identity_rule: There is one Prompt Kit website release. Local, portable, preview, installed, and public delivery surfaces must resolve to or derive from the exact canonical artifact; none may become an independent product version authority.

identity_evidence: canonical content SHA-256 with line endings normalized to LF
checkout-byte SHA-256 when validating a local derivative receipt
release_identity.content_hash_policy: Prompt Kit release-content SHA-256 normalizes CRLF and lone CR line endings to LF before hashing so Git checkout EOL conversion cannot create a false second release identity.
release_identity.worktree_hash_policy: Exact checkout-byte SHA-256 is diagnostic and is the correct comparator for a portable builder receipt produced from that checkout; it must not be compared across operating systems as the sole release identity.
release_identity.path_comparison_policy: Repository-relative identity paths normalize backslash to forward slash before comparison; Windows and POSIX separators do not create distinct artifact identities.
release_identity.version_label_policy: A visible vXX label is descriptive UI metadata only and never sufficient proof of release identity or freshness.

public_pages.required_behavior: publish the canonical artifact byte-for-byte from the Pages checkout/build

phone_launcher.required_behavior: route to the canonical public Prompt Kit; the launcher is not a second Prompt Kit

windows_portable.required_behavior: derive from the exact checked-out canonical artifact, record that checkout source SHA-256, normalize repository-relative path separators when validating identity, and add only the registered portability runtime

local_preview.required_behavior: serve the canonical artifact directly or a declared temporary derivative that records source identity; never use an unregistered local index.html as release authority

drift_failures: artifact registry points prompt-kit-website at a path other than web/prompt-kit/index.html
Pages publishes a Prompt Kit that is not compared byte-for-byte with web/prompt-kit/index.html in the executable Pages build step
portable/local generation uses a source other than web/prompt-kit/index.html
portable artifact receipt omits the checkout source SHA-256
a Windows backslash receipt path is treated as a different repository artifact than the same forward-slash path
a CRLF checkout is treated as a different release solely because its raw checkout-byte SHA-256 differs from a Linux LF checkout
freshness guidance treats a visible version label or old local copy as proof of currentness
documentation describes the local/portable site as a separate Prompt Kit version rather than a delivery derivative
an operator is told to guess which index.html is current instead of resolving prompt-kit-website through the artifact registry
an operator proof hard-codes a CI checkout-byte SHA-256 as a cross-platform invariant

failure_route.stale_or_different_local_surface: Mark the local surface stale-or-unverified, resolve prompt-kit-website from harness/artifacts.v1.json, prove branch and commit currentness, run the release-identity validator on that machine, rebuild or reacquire through the registered launcher, and compare normalized content identity plus local derivative receipt evidence before troubleshooting product behavior.
failure_route.cross_platform_hash_mismatch: Do not declare a second release from raw SHA mismatch alone. Compare normalized canonical content SHA-256, retain exact checkout-byte SHA-256 for local derivative receipt verification, and report both.
failure_route.public_surface_drift: Stop release claims, run builder parity and Pages contract validation, and repair the product/release lane; do not bless a second canonical artifact from the harness lane.

proof_ceiling: Repository contract proof that delivery surfaces name one canonical Prompt Kit content identity across Windows/POSIX separator and checkout-EOL conventions, plus executable Pages and portable-builder wiring. It does not prove a specific browser cache, service worker, deployed Pages response, installed app, or operator workstation currently displays the same release without runtime evidence.
